headline: Television turns pictures into signals that travel invisibly through space
universal_truth: Information can be transformed from one form to another without losing its meaning
fun_facts: Early TVs had only a few thousand pixels; modern 4K screens have over 8 million
The first television images were mechanical—a spinning disk with holes created the picture
Live TV travels from camera to your screen in a fraction of a second, often faster than sound travels across a stadium
discussion_questions: How has television changed what we know about the world?
What's different about seeing an event live versus recorded?
How does instant visual access to distant events change society?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Right now, invisible waves are passing through your body carrying pictures of events happening thousands of miles away. Television converts light into signals, sends them through the air, and recreates the picture in your home. Visual telepathy.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: A camera sees light, a TV screen makes light. In between, the picture becomes something else—a signal that can travel through wires or air. How does an image become a signal and back again?
cliff.prompt: How does a picture become a transmittable signal?

options.text: The picture is broken into data points describing each tiny section, transmitted as numbers or waves, then reassembled
options.response: Yes. The image is encoded as information—digital or analog—sent as signals, then decoded back into light patterns your eyes see as a picture.

options.text: Cameras capture a tiny version of the light and the TV enlarges it
options.response: Cameras don't send light itself—they convert light to information signals...

q1.title: Breaking It Down
q1.script: A TV picture is broken into thousands or millions of tiny dots—pixels. Each dot's color and brightness is encoded as data. This data can travel as radio waves, through cables, or over the internet. The TV reverses the process, lighting up each dot.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Breaking It Down"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Faster Than Sound
q2.script: Live TV can deliver images from a stadium to your screen faster than sound travels across that stadium. You might see a goal before the crowd's roar reaches people sitting in distant seats. Television moves at nearly the speed of light.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Window to the World
q3.script: Before television, most people never saw events beyond their immediate area. TV gave everyone a window to distant places—wars, moon landings, historic moments. What you could witness expanded from your neighborhood to the entire planet.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Information can transform without losing meaning. Television proves that pictures can become signals and back again—light to data to light. Meaning survives the journey through different forms.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 123. Tomorrow, we'll explore invisible waves carrying sound—radio. Until then, appreciate that the images on your screen traveled as invisible signals to reach your eyes.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Signal Appreciation - See the Transformation
growTrack.learning_objective: Appreciate the invisible infrastructure of visual media
growTrack.activity: When watching something on a screen, consider the journey: light hit a camera somewhere, became data, traveled through cables or air, and became light again on your screen. This invisible transformation happens constantly, connecting you to distant places.
